segments.text: AI is taking the world by storm.
It has superpowers that set it apart from any other software.
And the reason is simple.
AI is built on a completely different foundation.
To see how different it is,
consider how normal software is created.
A programmer sits down and writes code line by line,
creating a core set of rigid instructions called rules.
This flow chart shows an if-then-else statement,
like a login screen.
A user enters a password.
If the password matches, then it opens the app.
Else, it shows an error message.
Because this path is fixed, it never changes.
Written rules return the same result every time.
AI does not use a programmer's written rules
for every situation.
Instead, it relies entirely on patterns it learned
during its development.
This board breaks down the two phases behind every AI answer.
First is the training phase.
The model learns from enormous amounts of data,
turning countless examples into learned numerical patterns
before you ever use it.
Once trained, it answers one word at a time.
It uses probability to score
how likely each possible next word is
based on the word so far.
Then it chooses a likely next word,
adds it, and repeats the process.
Learn patterns first, use them to build every answer.
Think as normal software as a robot
perfectly executing a rigid recipe from a cookbook.
It makes the exact same dish every time.
AI is like a chef.
No one handed it a cookbook.
It cooked thousands of dishes,
recognized the patterns of flavor and heat,
and can now cook a completely novel dish
it has never made before.
This graphic shows that difference in action.
If you ask normal software,
what's the best game for my new PS5?
The programmed rule checks a preset list
and outputs the top entry.
Ask again, and it repeats the exact same answer.
Ask AI software that exact same prompt,
and it builds a fresh response
word by word using learned patterns.
You might get NHL 26 the second time
and God of War Ragnarok the third.
Rules repeat the programmed answer.
Patterns build a fresh one.
If you wanna calculate your GPA in a spreadsheet,
you enter your grades and credits
neatly into rows and columns.
That is structured data.
AI doesn't need this neatness.
It can process messy, real-world information,
like details scribbled on the back of a receipt
or buried in a copied text message.
That is unstructured data.
Think about drafting a lesson plan
from chaotic legal pad notes
filled with scratched lines and stray arrows.
Just taking a picture of that mess
doesn't give you a usable lesson document.
This diagram compares how both systems handle data.
Normal software forces you to fit information
into an expected structure,
relying entirely on specific fields,
file types, and commands it was built to handle.
AI software can look at those messy notes,
PDFs, or audio files,
make sense of the chaos,
and transform it into a summary or a clean first draft.
While the available inputs and outputs depend on the app,
the flexibility remains.
Normal software still wins
for exact, consistent jobs like GPA math,
but AI earns its place on the open-ended,
messy jobs that defy rigid rules.
So remember the rule.
You bring the mess, and AI helps make sense of it.
A human can hold kryptonite safely in a backpack,
but for Superman, it can be fatal.
AI's unique superpowers
come with their own specific kryptonite.
Because AI runs on patterns instead of rules,
trained behavior is harder to predict,
inspect, and lock down.
This board highlights the real-world risks
of unpredictability.
People use pattern building to generate scams that scale,
creating fake identities and convincing messages in seconds,
or deepfakes that target victims.
Even without malicious intent, AI can hallucinate.
It can sound highly confident
delivering medical or safety answers that are flat wrong.
The industry tries to manage these risks.
During training, they teach AI to avoid harmful behavior.
They also add a safety layer to the apps,
guardrails designed to block or redirect harmful requests.
But these safety measures are imperfect.
They can accidentally block harmless requests
or miss dangerous ones.
This graphic sums up the trade-off.
AI's foundation gives it new superpowers.
Those superpowers come with kryptonite.
